advice: Experiment: interleave updates to two independent reduction streams for each 2×2 output tile. Use all four FP32 ZA selectors as two partial accumulators per output quadrant: for each increasing k, update selectors 0–3 with the even-k terms and selectors 0–3 of a second tile are unavailable, so this cannot be done with only four tiles. Instead, use the four selectors for two independent column pairs within one row tile, but this reduces reuse. I do not recommend this schedule: four ZA tiles cannot hold two independent 2×2 accumulators, and splitting each output quadrant across alternating k values would change the reduction grouping. Abstain from proposing it as a legal experiment.
risks: The prior two-accumulator proposal has severe measured regression and should not be repeated unchanged. Pointer variants have inconclusive paired outcomes; they do not demonstrate a schedule benefit. With only four FP32 ZA tiles, a second independent accumulator set is unavailable. Splitting k into partial sums changes FP32 rounding order and can exceed the fixed 0.002 tolerance. No schedule change is justified by the supplied evidence while preserving the stated accumulator and reduction constraints.
